name: Exact decimal amount as sign, coefficient and scale
description: The amount is an exact decimal value: a sign, a non-negative integer coefficient and a scale expressed as a non-positive power of ten. Binary floating point is rejected as the canonical representation because it cannot represent common decimal fractions exactly. Digit bounds on coefficient and scale are declared by the host or profile, and a value that cannot be represented exactly at the declared scale is rejected rather than rounded away.

questions.text: What sign, integer coefficient and scale together represent the declared amount exactly?
answer_data: Scale as a non-positive power of ten

questions.text: Which exact encodings are permitted for the amount, and why is binary floating point excluded from them?
answer_data: Reference to the exactness requirement that excludes binary floating point

questions.text: What total-digit and fraction-digit bounds does the host or profile impose on this amount?
answer_data: Identifier of the profile that set them

questions.text: How is a supplied value rejected when it cannot be held exactly at the declared scale?
answer_data: Offending input token retained for diagnosis
Declared scale that the input violated

data_elements.name: Amount sign
data_elements.description: The sign component of the exact decimal value, kept distinct from the coefficient so that a signed zero remains expressible.

data_elements.name: Amount coefficient
data_elements.description: The non-negative integer coefficient of the exact decimal value, which together with the scale reconstructs the amount without loss.

data_elements.name: Declared amount scale
data_elements.description: The number of fraction digits carried by the declaration, declared explicitly rather than inferred from the currency code.

data_elements.name: Amount encoding declaration
data_elements.description: Which exact encoding carries the amount in a given projection, for example a decimal lexical string or an explicit coefficient-and-scale pair. Binary floating point is not an admissible value.

data_elements.name: Declared digit bounds
data_elements.description: The total-digit and fraction-digit limits the host or profile imposes on the amount, recorded so that a validator can reject out-of-bound values deterministically.

inline_only_rationale: The exact amount is a small set of scalar fields embedded directly in the host record; it has no independent existence, no separate retention life and no separate identity from the host object that declares it, so representing it as an artifact would fabricate an object that no source or projection recognizes.

name: Canonical lexical form, trailing zeros and zero handling
description: The canonical lexical form of the amount is fixed and distinct from any rendered display string. Because numerically equal decimal representations can differ visibly, the declaration must state whether trailing zeros are significant, and must state how zero and a signed zero are treated, so that round-tripping preserves sign, coefficient and scale.

questions.text: What is the canonical lexical form of this amount, and how does it differ from any string rendered for display?
answer_data: Rendered display string where one exists
Locale that produced the display string

questions.text: Are trailing zeros significant here, so that a value written with two fraction digits differs from the same value written with one?
answer_data: Policy for choosing among numerically equal representations

questions.text: How are zero and a signed negative zero distinguished, normalized or rejected in this declaration?
answer_data: Policy on accepting or normalizing a negative zero

questions.text: Which round-trip check proves that parsing and re-serializing preserves sign, coefficient and scale?

data_elements.name: Canonical amount string
data_elements.description: The amount in the model's canonical lexical form, with a single agreed treatment of sign, decimal point and zero padding, used for storage, hashing and equality.

data_elements.name: Rendered display string
data_elements.description: An optional human-facing rendering of the amount. Non-authoritative, locale-dependent, and never used for comparison or storage.

data_elements.name: Trailing-zero significance flag
data_elements.description: States whether the declared scale is meaningful in itself, so that numerically equal representations with different scales are not treated as identical.

data_elements.name: Negative-zero policy
data_elements.description: The declared policy for a zero coefficient carrying a negative sign: accepted as given, normalized to unsigned zero, or rejected.

inline_only_rationale: Canonical form, significance and zero policy are field-level rules and small inline values on the declaration itself. They are consumed at parse and serialization time and have no retained, separately addressable representation, so an artifact would misrepresent a formatting contract as a stored object.

name: Amount and currency inseparability on the host object
description: Amount, currency reference and declared scale form one indivisible declaration: published monetary datatypes bind them into a single type, and a value interchanged without a known currency code is not interpretable. The host object owns the business meaning, including what a negative amount signifies, and projections that split the parts into separate fields must still assert the binding.

questions.text: Which fields make up the indivisible declaration, and may any of them be stored or transmitted without the others?
answer_data: Atomicity rule and the prohibited partial forms

questions.text: Which host object and field declares this monetary value, and what meaning does the host assign to it?
answer_data: Host field path where the mixin is embedded

questions.text: What does a negative amount signify in this host context, and which signs are permitted at all?
answer_data: Permitted sign set for the field
Statement that the sign meaning is not derived from the currency

questions.text: How is the binding preserved when a target format splits amount and currency into separate fields?
answer_data: Assertion that reassembly reproduces the declaration

data_elements.name: Monetary declaration identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the monetary declaration instance, assigned by the adopting Dimension only where the host cannot address the declaration through its own record identity and field path.

data_elements.name: Host object and field reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the host record and the field path at which this mixin is embedded, establishing who owns the business meaning of the value.

data_elements.name: Host-declared sign semantics
data_elements.description: What the host says a negative amount means in this field, for example a credit, refund or reduction. Declared, never inferred from the currency or from the model.

data_elements.name: Permitted sign set
data_elements.description: The signs the host field admits, used to reject a negative value where the host permits only non-negative amounts.

inline_only_rationale: This finding describes an embedding contract between a mixin and its host record: the declaration lives inside the host's own persisted object and inherits the host's identity and lifecycle. There is nothing to retain independently, and creating an artifact would assert a standalone monetary record that this mixin explicitly is not.

name: Declared determinacy: exact point, interval, approximate or explicitly absent
description: A monetary field must be able to say what kind of assertion it is making. Published monetary vocabularies support a value or a bounded range, and published absent-value vocabularies distinguish unknown, masked, not-applicable, unsupported and error. The declaration therefore carries an explicit determinacy state, so an absent or unknown value is never silently expressed as zero and an interval is never collapsed to a point.

questions.text: Which determinacy state does this declaration assert: exact point value, interval, approximate value, unknown, missing or not applicable?
answer_data: State value from the declared vocabulary
Evidence or source of the state assertion

questions.text: Which rule forbids expressing an absent, unknown or not-applicable monetary value as zero?
answer_data: Absent-reason code carried instead of a numeric value
Validation outcome when a zero is supplied for an absent value

questions.text: When an interval is declared, which endpoints are present and is each endpoint inclusive or exclusive?
answer_data: Lower endpoint declaration or its absence
Upper endpoint declaration or its absence
Inclusivity flag for each present endpoint

questions.text: How is an interval checked for a shared currency reference and a consistent scale across both endpoints?
What must a consumer do when it cannot honour a declared approximate or absent state?
answer_data: Escalation path recorded for the unsupported state

data_elements.name: Value determinacy state
data_elements.description: The declared kind of monetary assertion: exact point value, interval, approximate value, or explicitly absent. Required so that no state is inferred from a numeric default.

data_elements.name: Absent-value reason
data_elements.description: When no amount is asserted, the reason for absence drawn from a declared vocabulary distinguishing unknown, masked, not applicable, unsupported and error.

data_elements.name: Interval lower endpoint
data_elements.description: The lower endpoint of a monetary interval, itself a complete monetary declaration carrying its own currency reference and scale.

data_elements.name: Interval upper endpoint
data_elements.description: The upper endpoint of a monetary interval, itself a complete monetary declaration carrying its own currency reference and scale.

data_elements.name: Endpoint inclusivity
data_elements.description: Whether each present interval endpoint is inclusive or exclusive, declared rather than assumed.

inline_only_rationale: Determinacy states, absent reasons and interval endpoints are inline field values plus references into a declared code vocabulary that another model or terminology authority publishes. Materializing them as an artifact would either duplicate that external vocabulary or invent a record with no counterpart in any consulted specification.

name: Rounding mode, increment, direction and tie handling
description: A quantization rule is interpretable only when mode, target exponent or increment, direction and tie handling are all stated. Accounting quantization to a currency minor unit, cash quantization to a non-decimal increment such as five cents, and custom contractual quantization are distinct named rules with different authorities and channel scopes — not variants of one default.

questions.text: Which named rounding mode applies to this value, and what authority establishes it?
answer_data: rounding mode identifier such as half-even, half-up, floor, ceiling, down, up or 05up
authority or legal instrument establishing the mode
jurisdiction or scheme scope of that authority

questions.text: Is the quantization target a power-of-ten scale or a non-decimal increment, and what exactly is that target?
answer_data: increment value with its currency for increment-based quantization
source of the target: currency minor unit, cash regime or contract

questions.text: How are exact half-way values resolved, and does the resolution differ by sign?
answer_data: tie rule such as half-up, half-even, half-down or away-from-zero
worked example for one positive and one negative tie

questions.text: Which payment or presentation channel does this quantization rule apply to, and which channels does it explicitly exclude?
answer_data: applicable channel: cash, electronic, accounting entry or display
scope: whole total only, or per line or component
voluntary or mandatory status of the rule

questions.text: How is a change to the quantization rule versioned so that historic amounts remain reproducible?
answer_data: reference to the superseded rule version
restatement policy for values produced under the earlier version

data_elements.name: Rounding mode
data_elements.description: Named rounding mode applied, drawn from the mandatory and optional decimal rounding modes rather than from a library default.

data_elements.name: Quantization increment
data_elements.description: Non-decimal increment to which the amount is quantized, expressed as an amount with a currency, for example a five-cent cash step.

data_elements.name: Target exponent
data_elements.description: Exponent the quantized result must carry when quantization is scale-based.

data_elements.name: Tie resolution rule
data_elements.description: How an exact half-way value is resolved, recorded explicitly because statutory and accounting defaults differ.

data_elements.name: Rule channel scope
data_elements.description: The channels and application points to which the rule applies and those it excludes.

artifacts.name: Quantization policy record
artifacts.description: A versioned, effective-dated record of one named quantization rule: mode, target exponent or increment, tie handling, channel scope, applicable currencies, and the instrument or authority that establishes it.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the issuing authority's instrument reference — a regulation, central-bank notice or scheme rule identifier — where one exists; otherwise by a governed IRI in the adopting Dimension's policy namespace; a UUID assigned by the Dimension only when neither exists. Version tokens and effective periods are attributes, never encoded into the identifier.

name: Calculation, settlement and display precision; intermediate versus final rounding
description: Distinct precision tiers apply at different stages. Intermediate calculation frequently requires more digits than the reporting minor unit, settlement quantizes to the payable increment, and presentation may differ again. Whether rounding is applied per component or once at the end changes the result, so the stage must be declared and results derived from already-rounded inputs must not be re-rounded silently.

questions.text: Which precision tiers are declared for this value, and what scale does each tier carry?
answer_data: tier list: calculation, settlement, presentation, reporting
the tier to which the recorded amount belongs

questions.text: At which points in the calculation was rounding applied, and was any intermediate result rounded?
answer_data: handling rule for components that were already rounded

questions.text: When a value is derived by conversion, what precision governs the conversion factor and the intermediate result?
answer_data: significant figures carried by the conversion factor
whether inverse or derived factors are permitted
minimum decimals retained in any intermediate amount
the single final quantization step applied to the result

questions.text: What is reported when a consumer requires a precision tier the producer did not declare?
answer_data: derivation rule reference where a tier is derived rather than refused

data_elements.name: Precision tier
data_elements.description: The declared tier or tiers this amount belongs to, such as calculation, settlement, presentation or reporting.

data_elements.name: Tier scale
data_elements.description: Scale or increment associated with each declared tier, allowing calculation precision to exceed reporting precision explicitly.

data_elements.name: Rounding stage
data_elements.description: The point at which rounding was applied: per component, at a named intermediate step, or once at the final result.

data_elements.name: Intermediate minimum decimals
data_elements.description: Minimum number of decimals that must be retained in an intermediate amount before the final quantization step.

inline_only_rationale: Precision tiers and rounding stages are parameters of the specific calculation that produced an amount; they are carried inline with the value and with the referenced quantization policy record. Emitting a separate artefact for every calculation would duplicate the host's process record without creating any independently governed object, and would imply this model owns the calculation itself.

name: Compatibility gate and host-supplied tolerance for comparison and aggregation
description: Equality, ordering and aggregation are defined only for values in a compatible context: identical currency binding, compatible valuation basis, and a stated rounding context. Equality must also state whether it compares numeric value alone or value and quantum together. Tolerance and materiality thresholds are supplied by the host or reporting framework; the mixin records which threshold was applied and refuses incompatible operations rather than converting implicitly.

questions.text: Which attributes must match before two monetary values may be compared or added?
answer_data: attributes deliberately ignored by the predicate

questions.text: Does equality compare numeric value only, or numeric value together with scale and exponent?
answer_data: documented consequence for sorting, deduplication and set membership

questions.text: What tolerance or materiality threshold applies to this comparison or reconciliation, and who set it?
answer_data: tolerance as an absolute amount with currency or as a proportion
threshold owner: host entity, reporting framework or scheme
instrument or policy reference for the threshold
scope over which the threshold applies

questions.text: What is returned when values are incompatible, and what must never happen implicitly?
answer_data: statement prohibiting implicit conversion and implicit re-quantization
the declared conversion the caller must perform and record first

questions.text: Under which single rounding and valuation context is an aggregate reported, and how is that context recorded with the result?
answer_data: rounding context selected for the aggregate
outcome of the member-value context check
context stamped onto the aggregate result

data_elements.name: Comparison context key
data_elements.description: Composite key of currency binding, valuation context and rounding context under which comparison, ordering or aggregation is permitted.

data_elements.name: Equality semantics selection
data_elements.description: Whether equality is numeric-value equality or value-and-quantum equality, recorded because numerically equal values may carry different exponents.

data_elements.name: Tolerance threshold
data_elements.description: Host-supplied absolute or proportional tolerance applied to a comparison or reconciliation check.

data_elements.name: Tolerance owner reference
data_elements.description: The party, framework or instrument that set the tolerance or materiality threshold.

data_elements.name: Incompatibility code

inline_only_rationale: This finding states preconditions, equality semantics and refusal reasons that travel with the value and its policy reference; the comparison itself is executed by the host runtime. Producing an artefact would imply this model owns evaluation results and their retention, which belong to the adopting Dimension's processing and audit layers.

data_elements.name: Rate type code

inline_only_rationale: Source, methodology and series key are references into a publication model that owns the rate series and its determination. Holding them as attributes keeps the boundary intact; creating a local artifact would begin to mirror the publisher's record and would drift from the authoritative series.

description: Records the exact equation applied — including whether the rate was multiplied or divided and in which order chaining and rounding occurred — the target minor unit and rounding mode, and the tolerance within which a recomputation must reproduce the stored converted amount.

answer_data: Equation expression in an unambiguous notation
Operand bindings to the original amount and each rate reference
Statement of the direction convention the equation assumes

questions.text: In which order were conversion, chaining and rounding applied?
answer_data: Ordered list of computation and rounding steps
Points at which precision was reduced
Whether component amounts were rounded before or after aggregation

questions.text: To which minor unit or decimal precision was the converted amount rounded, and under which rounding mode?
answer_data: Target currency minor unit from the ISO 4217 register
Declared accuracy of the converted amount and whether it is exact or rounded

answer_data: Flagging and escalation behaviour on breach

data_elements.name: Conversion equation expression
data_elements.description: Unambiguous expression of the computation applied, with explicit operand roles and rate direction.

data_elements.name: Rounding mode code
data_elements.description: Coded rounding mode applied at each reduction of precision.

data_elements.name: Rounding step order
data_elements.description: Ordered record of computation and rounding steps, showing where precision was reduced.

data_elements.name: Target currency minor unit
data_elements.description: Minor unit exponent of the target currency taken from the ISO 4217 register version applicable at the valuation instant.

data_elements.name: Converted amount value
data_elements.description: Exact decimal result of the conversion, stored with its declared accuracy and without any scaling multiplier.

data_elements.name: Recomputation tolerance
data_elements.description: Permitted residual difference between an independent recomputation and the stored converted amount.

inline_only_rationale: The equation, rounding order and tolerance are the executable specification of the stored number and must be readable as fields by any agent attempting recomputation. They are bundled into the evidence artifact only as part of a complete reproduction package, not held separately as a document here.

name: Host-dependent weak identity of a monetary assertion
description: A monetary value has no independent existence: it is identified by its host record, the role it plays on that host, its currency and its valuation context, mirroring how a reported monetary fact is identified by concept, context and unit. A valuation date is context, never an identifier.

questions.text: Which combination of host reference, role on the host, currency and valuation context uniquely identifies this monetary assertion?
Under which conditions must the adopting Dimension mint a surrogate identifier instead of relying on the host key?
How is this assertion distinguished from another that merely carries the same amount and the same currency?
Is the monetary assertion an inseparable component of the host record or a separately addressable record?

data_elements.name: Host record reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the record the monetary value is attached to; mandatory because the mixin has no standalone existence.

data_elements.name: Role on host
data_elements.description: Code for the position the value occupies on its host (for example gross amount, tax amount, translated amount), which discriminates same-valued siblings.

data_elements.name: Identity component set
data_elements.description: Ordered list naming the attributes that jointly identify the assertion (host reference, role, currency, valuation context), used for collision checks.

data_elements.name: Dimension-assigned surrogate identifier
data_elements.description: UUID or ULID minted only when the host key is unavailable or unstable; never derived from a date.

inline_only_rationale: Identity here is a key definition and a set of pointer fields evaluated at read time. Emitting an artifact would create a second, competing identity anchor for something that is deliberately dependent on its host, and would invite systems to treat the monetary value as an independent master record.

name: Deterministic as-of read of a bound monetary assertion
description: The rules that make a read reproducible: which two instants the caller supplies, which single version those instants select, what must be returned unchanged, and how an unresolvable, absent or retired result is reported. A monetary amount carries an explicit validity interval rather than an implied always-current value, so a read without an as-of pair is under-specified.

questions.text: Which effective instant and which observation cut-off instant does a read supply, and what is the declared default when either is omitted?
answer_data: Requested effective (valuation) instant as an RFC 3339 value with seconds and an explicit offset or Z
Requested observation/ingestion cut-off instant in the same form
Declared defaults, for example effective = request instant and observation = latest recorded
Statement of whether a caller-supplied offset is preserved or normalised, and which form is used for comparison

questions.text: Which single assertion version is selected when more than one effective interval covers the requested instant, and how is a tie broken?
answer_data: Ordered list of candidate versions with their effective intervals
Interval boundary convention (inclusive start, exclusive end) and the containment test applied
Deterministic tie-break key, for example latest observation instant then highest version counter
Explicit none-applicable outcome marker used instead of returning the nearest version

questions.text: Which stored values must a read return verbatim, and which derivations are forbidden in the read path?
answer_data: Amount returned as the stored canonical decimal string including trailing zeros, with the declared scale
Currency code returned as stored, plus the register list and status that applied at the effective instant
Prohibition on conversion, re-scaling, rounding or unit substitution during a read
Flag raised when the stored currency code is historic or withdrawn at the effective instant

questions.text: How does a read report an unresolvable host binding, a tombstoned assertion, or an as-of request outside the supported range?
answer_data: Structured failure descriptor with a resolvable type URI, title, status, detail and instance
Distinct codes for unknown identifier, unresolvable binding, tombstoned assertion and unsupported as-of window
Gone-style outcome for a tombstoned assertion, kept distinct from unknown-identifier
Reference to the advisory eligibility report when a value is withheld rather than absent

data_elements.name: Requested effective instant
data_elements.description: The valuation instant for which the caller wants the monetary assertion resolved.

data_elements.name: Requested observation cut-off instant
data_elements.description: The recording-time cut-off; versions recorded after this instant are excluded, allowing a past view of what was known at a given time.

data_elements.name: Version selection trace
data_elements.description: Ordered record of candidate versions considered, the containment test result for each, and the tie-break key applied, sufficient to reproduce the selection.

data_elements.name: Resolution outcome code
data_elements.description: Coded result of the read: resolved, none-applicable, unresolvable-binding, tombstoned or withheld.

data_elements.name: Currency register status at effective instant
data_elements.description: Which maintenance-agency list the referenced code belonged to at the effective instant: current currency, fund code or historic/withdrawn.

inline_only_rationale: An as-of read is a deterministic projection computed over assertion versions the host already persists; it creates no new governed content. Emitting a stored artifact for every read would produce a second, divergent copy of a host-owned record and would imply ownership of persistence and of audit-trail production, both of which belong to the host and to the audit component respectively. The read therefore exists only as inline request parameters plus reference values — the selected version identifier, its validator, and the outcome code — with no artifact of its own.

name: Quantisation, rounding policy and residual
description: How an exact amount is brought to a target scale: the target scale (usually but not always the currency minor unit), the rounding mode and tie-breaking rule, the resulting residual, and how a residual is allocated when a total is split across components so that the parts still sum to the whole. Precision loss is an explicit, declared outcome rather than an invisible side effect.

questions.text: What rounding policy — target scale, rounding mode and tie-breaking rule — governs quantisation of this amount?
answer_data: order of quantisation relative to other operations

questions.text: What residual arises from quantisation, and how is it computed, reported or allocated across components?
When may the target scale differ from the currency minor unit, and which authority pins that deviation?
answer_data: scope in which the deviation is valid

questions.text: How is precision loss detected and expressed so that a consumer knows the value is no longer exact?

data_elements.name: Declared scale
data_elements.description: The number of fractional digits to which the amount is stated, which may equal the currency minor unit or a pinned deviation from it.

data_elements.name: Rounding mode and tie rule
data_elements.description: The rounding mode applied and the tie-breaking rule used when a value falls exactly half-way, stated explicitly because regimes differ.

data_elements.name: Quantisation residual
data_elements.description: The signed difference between the exact input amount and the quantised result, expressed in the same currency.

data_elements.name: Implied value interval
data_elements.description: The interval of plausible source values implied by the declared decimals and rounding mode of a quantised amount, used later for tolerance evaluation.

data_elements.name: Exactness indicator
data_elements.description: Whether the stated amount is exact or the product of a lossy quantisation.

artifacts.name: Rounding policy profile
artifacts.description: A declarative, versioned profile stating target scale rules per currency or context, rounding mode, tie-breaking rule, residual allocation method and the order of quantisation relative to conversion. It is referenced by derivations so that a historical result remains reproducible after the policy changes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative identifier issued by the adopting Dimension's policy registry plus an immutable version identifier; where no registry identifier exists, a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. The effective-from instant is an attribute, never the identifier.

artifacts.name: Quantisation record
artifacts.description: The reportable result of one quantisation: exact input amount and currency, target scale, applied policy profile reference, quantised output, signed residual, exactness indicator and implied value interval.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identifier of the operation invocation supplied by the caller if it has one; otherwise a ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, bound to the content hash of the input amount, policy reference and output.
